Description

These evil beings crawled up from subterranean depths long ago. Their concentrating magical power lets them use multiple spells at once.

Defense

AC 18, touch 11, flat-footed 16 (+2 Dex, +7 natural, -1 size)

hp 51 [78] (6d10+18)

mp 14

Fort +8, Ref +4, Will +8

DR 5/cold iron or good;

Immune lightning, poison;

Resist Fire 15, Ice 10, Earth 10;

SR 16

Weakness holy

Offense

Speed 40 ft., fly 90 ft. (good)

Melee Mwk longsword +9/+4 (2d6+5/19-20), Mwk whip +9 (1d4+2) or 2 Slams +10 (2d6+5)

Space 10 ft.; Reach 10 ft. (30 ft. with whip)

Special Attacks Concentrating Magical Power

Spells Known (FC CL 6th; Concentration +9)

1st (DC 14) - Blizzard, Dark, Fire, Thunder

2nd (DC 15) - Blizzard II, Dark II, Fire II, Thunder II

Statistics

Str 20, Dex 15, Con 17, Int 8, Wis 16, Cha 12

Base Atk +6 CMB +12 CMD 24

Feats Combat Reflexes, Improved Natural Attack (Slam), Two-Weapon Fighting

Skills Acrobatics +11, Bluff +10, Fly +13, Perception +20, Sense Motive +12; Racial Modifiers +8 Perception

Languages Abyssal; telepathy 100 ft.

SQ Whip Mastery

description.unidentified:
A whip deals no damage to any creature with an armor bonus of +1 or higher or a natural armor bonus of +3 or higher. The whip is treated as a melee weapon with a 15-foot reach, though you don't threaten the area into which you can make an attack. In addition, unlike most other weapons with reach, you can use it against foes anywhere within your reach (including adjacent foes).

Using a whip provokes an attack of opportunity, just as if you had used a ranged weapon.

You can use the Weapon Finesse feat to apply your Dexterity modifier instead of your Strength modifier to attack rolls with a whip sized for you, even though it isn't a light weapon. You can't wield a whip in two hands in order to apply 1-1/2 times your Strength modifier to damage rolls.
